food_cultures.name_en: Okunitama Shrine Chestnut Festival and Musashino Chestnuts
food_cultures.summary_en: Fuchu's autumn chestnut festival preserves the memory of Musashino's historical chestnut production and offerings to the Tokugawa rulers.

facts.claim_en: Tokyo's official tourism site explains that chestnuts were a valued Musashino crop and that their harvest became associated with Okunitama Shrine's autumn festival.
facts.source_title: 大國魂神社―秋季祭・くり祭―
facts.publisher: 東京観光財団 GO TOKYO

facts.claim_en: Fuchu city identifies the chestnut festival as a surviving reminder of the Musashino plateau's historical chestnut-growing culture.
facts.source_title: 府中市の秋の行事（9～11月）

places.relation_en: Historic setting of the chestnut festival and its harvest-related traditions.

food_cultures.notes_en: This primarily documents a historical crop and living festival tradition, not substantial contemporary commercial chestnut farming within the municipality.

food_cultures.summary_en: Kozuru is Fuchu's historic local sake, closely connected with Musashi Province's former administrative center and Okunitama Shrine.

facts.claim_en: Noguchi Brewery traces its origins to 1860, when the family began brewing sacred sake connected with Okunitama Shrine.
facts.source_title: 武蔵府中の地酒 國府鶴

facts.claim_en: The brewery reports that local sake production resumed at its own Fuchu facility in spring 2024 after an earlier period of outsourced brewing.
facts.source_title: 武蔵府中の地酒 國府鶴

makers.relation_en: Brewer of Kozuru sake.

food_cultures.notes_en: The site's history distinguishes the brewery's establishment from the 2024 resumption of production in Fuchu.
